headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and broad-egress pair: Cursor can ingest Cognee outputs and act on them with write/network privileges.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs, while Cognee can produce documents/data/workflows that may be copied or written into shared files. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge even though no direct shared channel is explicitly documented between these two products. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Cognee output is pasted into Cursor buffers or saved into a shared workspace file
IF Cursor treats file or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools
Keep Cognee outputs in a separate directory not opened by Cursor
Require manual review before Cursor executes any instructions from files
Use a provenance tag or prefix for Cognee-generated text
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; Cursor reads workspace files/open buffers and can send content to model providers and MCP servers. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive data can flow from Cognee-managed content into Cursor's outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF Cognee stores sensitive records in a workspace that Cursor opens
IF Cursor forwards open-file contents or buffers to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Separate sensitive Cognee data from Cursor workspaces
Turn off or restrict MCP servers for the Cursor session
Use a redaction step before opening files in Cursor
Limit Cursor to local-only models for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; Cognee has session memory and allowlisted egress. If they share a directory or project, Cursor can overwrite or mutate Cognee-managed artifacts and git state without locking. The overlap is operationally dangerous and defaults are not isolated enough to rule it out.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode or otherwise writes without external locking
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate working directory
Disable Yolo mode for shared repos
Use git worktrees or branches with explicit locks
Make Cognee outputs read-only to Cursor
requires-engineering: add cross-agent file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can act on files, shell, and git changes, so Cognee-generated decisions or workflow text can become authoritative input that Cursor executes or commits. Cognee's support and finance data context increases the chance that a mistaken downstream action has real impact. Because Cursor's action-taking authority is explicit, the cascade is severe.
conditions: IF Cursor uses Cognee output as a source of truth without verification
IF Cursor is allowed to execute shell commands or commit git changes based on that output
mitigations: Require human approval before execution or commit
Add a verification step against source data before acting
Restrict Cursor to read-only review mode for Cognee outputs
Log and diff all generated actions before applying them
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Cursor can upload workspace contents to external model providers and MCP servers. If regulated data is opened in Cursor, residency or retention obligations may be harder to satisfy than in Cognee alone. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their interaction, not either one in isolation.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is present in files opened by Cursor
IF Cursor routes those files to third-party model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from Cursor workspaces
Use a DPA-approved model/provider configuration
Disable MCP servers for regulated projects
Shorten retention in the provider settings if available
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls
